title: umbra
body:
every once in a while i find myself surrounded
by an audience of street lamps
shooting their photon bullets
from their scrutinizing gaze.

they contort and
stretch my figure
until it barely resembles the body from which it came.

they project rings
of jet black serpents and nymphs and demons
dancing and bending
as I'm followed by their rays.

part of me wishes I could join their ritualistic disco.
part of me wonders what they dance for, but
before I unravel their mystery
they vanish over the horizon of the dance floor.

and when my last shadowed comrades
melt away
all that remains is a lonely figure
in a forest of incandescent bulbs
humming like mosquitos
drawing the blood from my veins
leaving a white caricature too lazy
to refine his own contour so
I lay there
like a chalk outline at a crime scene where
no crime was committed to any
known eyes but the ones
I used to have.
